claims.text: NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center Advisory Number 19 (11 PM HST, Thursday, 24 September 2026) placed Hurricane Nolo at 15.5N 155.6W, about 240 miles south of South Point, Hawaii, with maximum sustained winds of 80 mph (130 km/h) and a minimum central pressure of 985 mb, moving north-northeast at 5 mph; 'additional strengthening is forecast, and Nolo is expected to become a major hurricane on Saturday,' with a turn toward the west-northwest and west forecast Saturday and Sunday.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Hawaiʻi
claims.text: The Office of the Governor of Hawaii announced the closure of state and county offices, public schools and University of Hawaii campuses and facilities on Hawaii Island for Thursday, September 24 and Friday, September 25, 2026, with closures expanding to Maui County on Friday, September 25, as the state prepared for potentially dangerous impacts -- heavy rain, damaging winds and flooding -- from Tropical Storm Nolo.

Hawaii County Mayor Mitchell D. Roth issued an Emergency Proclamation Relating to Tropical Storm Nolo after the National Weather Service's Central Pacific Hurricane Center issued Tropical Storm Nolo Advisory Number 13 on 23 September 2026, with Nolo centered about 310 miles south of South Point, Hawaii Island, maximum sustained winds near 40 mph, and forecast to approach Hawaii Island on Friday and Saturday, September 25 and 26, 2026, under a Hurricane Watch issued by the National Weather Service for the County.

NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center Advisory Number 23 (11 PM HST, Friday, 25 September 2026) placed Hurricane Nolo about 145 miles south of South Point, Hawaii, with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (165 km/h), nearly stationary but forecast to move westward with increasing speed over the weekend, then turn north-northwest; the advisory states Nolo 'will strengthen into a major hurricane on Saturday and peak in intensity by late Sunday,' with a Hurricane Watch in effect for Hawaii County, a Tropical Storm Warning for Hawaii County, and a Tropical Storm Watch for Maui County, and 8 to 12 inches of rain (isolated 16 inches) expected on the Big Island's eastern and southern slopes.

NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center Advisory Number 27 (11 PM HST, Saturday, 26 September 2026) placed Hurricane Nolo at 16.5N 157.3W, about 200 miles south-southwest of South Point, Hawaii, with maximum sustained winds of 100 mph (155 km/h); 'there are no coastal watches or warnings in effect' for Hawaii, though watches may be required for portions of the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument.

description: Hurricane Nolo strengthened into a Category 2 storm south of Hawaii's Big Island in late September 2026, prompting a state of emergency and county-level emergency proclamation ahead of a forecast major-hurricane approach. NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center's Advisory 27 (11 PM HST, 26 September) placed Nolo about 200 miles south-southwest of South Point with 100 mph winds, moving away from Hawaii with no coastal watches or warnings remaining in effect. Hawaii's governor and Hawaii County's mayor had declared emergencies, closed state and county offices and schools on Hawaii Island and Maui County, and warned of catastrophic, life-threatening flash flooding from forecast rainfall of 8 to 12 inches (isolated totals to 16 inches); no casualties or damage have been confirmed by an authoritative source, and the direct threat to Hawaii has passed as the storm tracks west into open ocean.

impact.summary: NOAA's Central Pacific Hurricane Center Advisory 27 (11 PM HST, 26 September 2026) placed Nolo as a Category 2 hurricane with 100 mph maximum sustained winds, located about 200 miles south-southwest of South Point, Hawaii, and moving away to the west with no coastal watches or warnings in effect for Hawaii. At its closest approach the storm brought strong winds, heavy rain and large surf to the Big Island and Maui County, prompting a state of emergency, county emergency proclamation, and closures of state/county offices and schools, but no confirmed deaths, injuries or damage have been published by an authoritative source. Nolo is forecast to continue strengthening into a major hurricane over open ocean, away from Hawaii.

location.region: Hawaii Island (Big Island) and Maui County, Hawaii

event.scale: Category 2 hurricane at closest approach to Hawaii; no landfall

name: Hurricane Nolo, Hawaii

updates.text: NOAA Advisory 27 (26 Sept, 11 PM HST) placed Nolo ~200 miles south-southwest of South Point with 100 mph winds; no coastal watches or warnings remain in effect for Hawaii as the storm moves away to the west.

Nolo intensified to a Category 2 hurricane (105 mph) per NOAA Advisory 23, still forecast to reach major hurricane strength by Saturday and peak late Sunday; a Hurricane Watch is now in effect for Hawaii County.
